claim_scope: Known no-change managed live-root release and its settlement verifier. A no-change release is written only by the real lease close, after a rescan of the held live root equals the Store baseline tree digest. The settlement verifier accepts it only when this run's durable seed record carries the same tree digest and sits between admission and release. Verified through the real lease close, a real sessionrepo Store, and a file-backed audit journal; the registration verifier is the existing test seam. Re-verified in a fresh process at the settlement verifier. Not claimed: public catalog verification of a NO_DIFF receipt, admission of a new request ID through the SQLite catalog, the production D09 registration path, or a full production session run. For NO_DIFF, receipt Success means a verified clean runtime completion status for a no-change run; it is not evidence of task success.

defect_addressed.summary: R1 accepted a no-change release on device/inode identity, the admission and release records, and the ledger anchor. It recorded no content digest at release and did not bind the release to a durable seed digest. Its positive fixture handwrote the release record rather than calling close. Net-reverted runs (changes whose composed delta is empty) still went to Finalize, which produced a zero-object Succeeded publication that the verifier could not accept.
defect_addressed.identity_is_not_content_proof: Device, inode, and mount identity are retained as before. Content equality is proven by two endpoint tree digests, admitted and released, with the Store baseline and workspace policy.

change.managed_live_root_linux.go: Release record gains released_tree_digest (omitempty). markNoPublication(options, baseline) records the Store baseline generation and policy. close() for outcome no-publication rescans the held root with workspace.Scan (Generation = baseline ID, QuiescentRoot true, Store policy) and fails closed with ErrManagedLiveRootRetained unless the digest equals the baseline digest; the digest is written to the release record. Fences, the one-use permit, and begin() are unchanged.
change.production_session_linux.go: NO_DIFF branch is selected by bundleHasNoChange: no approved transition carries a change, or the verified ValidatedChain sealed tree equals the verified baseline tree (both valid digests). That branch calls markNoPublication(session.Workspace, session.Generation). The Finalize zero-object NO_DIFF branch is unchanged from HEAD; it is unreachable with a changed sealed tree and its receipt Success stays false.
change.production_workflow_catalog_linux.go: verifyManagedPiNoPublicationSettlement also calls verifyManagedNoChangeSeed: exactly one managed_root_source_capture_seeded record for this run, strict decode, schema_version, run_id, generation_id g0, and tree_digest equal to the release's released_tree_digest, with its sequence strictly between admission and release. Settlement ID is unchanged: no-publication plus the release record hash.
change.production_workflow_catalog_linux_test.g: R1 handwritten no-publication fixture removed. R1 receipt-claim and empty-provider tests kept.
change.production_no_change_linux_test.go (new): Real lease fixture: real sessionrepo Store; seeding through seedManagedRootSourceWithProof (the Store.Seed negative is unseeded); real acquire, completeAdmissionRecovery, markNoPublication, and close; file-backed audit journal. Fresh-process verification runs the settlement verifier in a child test binary that opens the journal cold; the child writes a result file and the parent fails if it is missing or mismatched. Hand-written release records are used only for tamper cases, and a matching hand-written record in the close shape is accepted first. The routing predicate has its own table test.

open_objections: The public catalog verifier and new-ID admission through the SQLite catalog are not proved. This is the main remaining part of the R1 goal.

The release-time content proof compares two endpoint scans: identity plus equal digests at seed and at release. A change that reverts before release is not detected, so the lease fence is the only protection in between.
Routing net-reverted runs to the no-publication release instead of Finalize is a behavior change for those runs. PUBLISHED behavior is unchanged: a changed sealed tree still goes to Finalize.

The Finalize zero-object NO_DIFF branch is kept verbatim from HEAD. It is unreachable by construction: a changed sealed tree composes at least one change and makePlans emits one plan per composed change, so a succeeded publication has an object. The parent should decide whether to delete it or keep it as a dead guard.
The owner-incarnation guard failure from R1 did not recur in the two module runs of a3 (workflowrecovery ok in both). It is not proved fixed, and the guard was not changed.
